Virtually Reborn Ford Thunderbird Super Coupe Steals the CGI Soul of a Mighty Aston Martin Valen
7 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
The Ford Motor Company has been pretty busy lately – Ford Racing has a new Global Director, the Blue Oval is now in the battery business, launched the Ford Custom Garage Maverick SV300T package, and also introduced us to the Mustang GTD 1901, which pays tribute to Henry Ford’s original race car.
Ford Racing’s new Global Director is Pascal Zurlinden, as the subsidiary “grows into a broader global business, connecting what it learns in competition to the vehicles and experiences it creates for customers.” The Blue Oval has also joined the battery-making business, with cells coming off the line at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan in Marshall as they go to the Louisville plant to enter the packs of the new Ford Fathom EV pickup truck.
As far as the model novelties are concerned, Ford Custom Garage launched the limited-edition SV300T package recently in two configurations – Black or Bronze – bringing both Ford Accessories and Ford Racing Parts together on the 2025 and 2026 Maverick XLT, Lariat, and Lobo models packing the 2.0-liter EcoBoost engine and all-wheel drive, now rocking 300 horsepower under the hood.
While all fans wait for the Ford Mustang GTD Competition upgrade, the Ford Motor Company actually introduced the 2028 model year Mustang GTD with the 1901 livery , which pays its respects to Henry Ford’s first 1901 two-cylinder race car. The company itself wasn’t even founded back then, so Ford Racing is technically older (125 years) than its parent enterprise.
As such, with all the commotion around the Blue Oval, we’re not surprised that the rumor mill and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators are keeping an eye on everything Ford. Just recently, someone stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to focus on a fresh Ford. Or an Aston Martin. Or both…
More precisely, Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm and dreams of a FoMoCo idea – again. He recently crafted things like the rumored, upcoming S650 Ford Mustang Cobra, a return of the Crown Victoria sedan, and even a Mercury Cougar XR7 along with a Ford Taurus SHO.
But now he’s taking the unofficial, hypothetical design projects to new heights – up there on cloud number nine alongside ultra-luxury and exotic creations like the recent Aston Martin Valen. The latter is a new grand tourer by the British automaker that’s powered by a 5.2-liter AE31 twin-turbo V12 shared with the third-generation Vanquish, rocking for this application no less than 838 hp (625 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,001 Nm) of torque.
Alas, the pixel master sees its front end as quite similar to the shape of the fascia of 1960s Ford T-Birds, which is why he decided to CGI mash the Valen with the Ford aura to attempt to create a fresh Thunderbird Super Coupe. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)
